input: Order custom stamps for my vintage mail correspondence

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Custom stamps can mean postage-valid stamps (e.g., via USPS Photo Stamps or Zazzle), decorative wax seals, rubber stamps, or embossed stickers — each requires a completely different vendor and process.
Whether these stamps are for personal use, a business, a wedding, or gifting affects quantity, branding needs, and the level of personalisation required.
The specific vintage style (Victorian, Art Deco, 1950s retro, etc.) and imagery (monogram, botanical, postmark motif) directly determines the design direction and which vendors can deliver it.
Budget per stamp or total order budget determines whether to use a premium bespoke service or a mass-print platform, and how many stamps can realistically be ordered.
The quantity needed drives minimum order requirements and vendor eligibility, since some services have high minimums while others sell in small sheets.
Whether there is a deadline (e.g., upcoming event, wedding invitations going out) determines urgency, rush-order options, and whether standard production timelines are feasible.

Knowing whether the stamps must be postally valid for actual mailing vs. purely decorative (for aesthetics, sealing, or journaling) is the single biggest filter for which products and vendors to consider.

gold.taskTitle: Order custom stamps for vintage mail correspondence
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to purchase custom-designed stamps to use on physical mail that fits a vintage aesthetic.

questions.title: Should the stamps be valid for actual postage?
questions.description: Determine whether the stamps need to be officially valid for mailing letters (e.g., USPS-approved photo stamps) or whether they can be purely decorative, such as rubber stamps, wax seals, or sticker labels.

questions.title: What specific vintage era or style should the design reflect?
questions.description: Identify the aesthetic direction — Victorian, Art Deco, 1920s postmark, 1950s retro, floral botanical, etc. — to guide vendor and design choices.

questions.title: Who is this correspondence for — personal, business, or an event?
questions.description: Clarify whether the stamps are for everyday personal letters, a brand or business identity, or a specific occasion like a wedding or party invitation.

questions.title: How many stamps do you need to order in total?
questions.description: Establish the required quantity, as this determines which vendors are eligible (many have minimum order requirements) and affects per-unit cost.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this stamp order?
questions.description: Understand the spending limit to filter between premium bespoke design services and more affordable mass-print platforms.

questions.title: Do you have a deadline for when the stamps must arrive?
questions.description: Determine whether there is a hard date driving urgency, which would require factoring in production lead times and whether rush shipping is needed.

questions.title: Do you already have artwork, or does a design need to be created?
questions.description: Find out if the user has ready-to-upload artwork or needs help sourcing a designer or using a vendor's built-in design tool, which affects the steps and timeline.
